messages:
Maya (PM): heads up — competitor launched a low-cost 'lite' inference tier. keynote customer (Acme) pinged us asking if we can match latency/cost for their bulk preview use-case. rough ask: ~30–50ms p95 for short prompts, ~40% lower cost than our hosted default.
Ana (Sales): they said it's blocking their procurement. their engineering wants a deterministic SLA for previews. they explicitly said they don't need streaming or function-calls in the lite mode.
TJ (Eng): thanks. a few clarifying q's: 1) target qps? 2) payload lengths? 3) quality tolerance? can we get the exact competitor bench?
Ana (Sales): Acme: typical batch is 4–8 tokens, 10k previews/day during peak. they want 99.5 availability, soft on exact RL fidelity (they mostly use short completions).
Liam (Data): pulled some public benchmarks + quick crawl of competitor docs: they advertise 35ms p95 on 1–2 token replies for a small model variant. on our telemetry, short prompts are currently 70ms p95 on hosted medium plan for same seq len.
Sam (Eng-ML): two quick paths: (A) product-lite = smaller model (7B) + int8 quant + tuned kernel + aggressive batching; preserves latency but quality risk; (B) feature-gated optimization on current models (prefix caching + microbatching) — less risk to quality but more infra work.
Claire (Research): for any parity attempt, propose these acceptance criteria:
- quality: intent-preservation >= 95% vs baseline on our preview prompt set (we have 120 examples)
- latency: p95 <= 50ms for <= 8 token responses at pilot load
- cost: per-token spend <= 0.6x current hosted default (target 40% reduction)
If we fail quality, we should fall back to default model.
TJ (Eng): ops caveat: microbatching helps throughput but adds variance; to hit p95 we likely need kernel-level ops + smaller model. also KV cache memory pressure on multi-tenant pools is real. fallback policy needs to be instant.
Maya (PM): thinking product path: ship a "Preview Lite" offering that intentionally disables streaming, function-calls, and long-context. lower tier with pinned 7B quantized model. launch as closed-beta with Acme. thoughts?
Sam (Eng-ML): implement spike plan:
```
- quantize candidate 7B -> int8
- run smoke perf: 1 node, 500 rps, 8 token replies
- measure p50/p95/p99 and run eval set for quality drift
```
Expect ~2 engineers for 2 weeks for the spike + 2 weeks to harden canary.
Liam (Data): I'll run the eval set and add an A/B script. quality check will compute intent-preservation and token-diff rates. I can share results in 3–4 days after spike.
TJ (Eng): operational checklist (short):
- capacity pool (dedicated lite GPUs)
- autoscale guard rails and burst cap
- instant fallback route to default model (per-request)
- per-tenant throttle and quota separate from default
- cost-metering tags
I'll tag infra for queue.
deploy-bot: scheduled capacity check for lite pool tomorrow 09:00 UTC
Ana (Sales): Acme is OK with closed-beta, they'll take the canary as long as SLA is explicit and we give a rollback plan.
Maya (PM): decision proposal: prioritize a limited-scope lite tier that restricts features but targets competitor latency/cost. launch criteria = Claire's three acceptance metrics + canary on Acme traffic at 10% for 2 weeks. dev estimate: 4–6 weeks to pilot.
TJ (Eng): +1 but add infra lead time. if we compress timeline, quality risk increases.
Claire (Research): we'll provide stepwise pass/fail gates. if intent-preservation < 95% we stop rollout.
Maya (PM): OK — action items: Sam spike (start Mon), Liam eval harness, TJ infra provisioning, Ana coordinate Acme canary. sync Wed 11:00 to review spike data. I'll file a short PRD and link here. :thumbsup:
Sam (Eng-ML): noted. starting spike Monday. will drop initial numbers in the channel.
Liam (Data): will prep the evaluation rubric and A/B harness.
TJ (Eng): will open infra ticket and assign owners.
Maya (PM): thanks team — trying to keep parity footprint minimal so we keep clear differentiators elsewhere (streaming/advanced tools). we won't commit to full parity on function-calls for now. meeting Wed 11.
deploy-bot: created ticket INFRA-7894 for lite-pool provisioning.
